title: Ampersand: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Flight Strip Bay. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Flight Strip Bay
options.lineage: Air traffic control flight progress strips in a strip bay
options.thesis: Every running command is a strip in the controller's bay: read at a glance, handled by hand, never lost.
materials: printed strip card in a coloured holder
options.viewport: Popover = the strip bay: one strip per command, a coloured holder edge for state, fixed fields (name, port, CPU, mem, uptime) in ruled boxes; groups are separate bays.
options.risk: Becomes costume if strips get fake paper texture; must stay flat, native, and dense.

raised.raise: State lives in the holder's form, not only its hue: solid = running, dashed = restarting, struck = stopped, doubled = crashed.
Every strip shares one fixed-field grid, so columns line up across bays like a printed form.
Every command carries a job number (%1, %2…) as its callsign and its ⌘-number shortcut.
Load reads as one ranked magnitude glyph per strip instead of two competing number columns.

regions.label: footer: + Add · Open window · Quit (stops all)

options.label: Job Control Table
options.thesis: Ampersand looks like the `jobs` command grew a UI: typographic rows, state words, nothing else.
options.viewport: Popover is a `jobs` table: [n]+ marker, state word, command line truncated, port and load right-aligned.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for a dev tool; can read like a terminal screenshot rather than a Mac app.

regions.label: header row: JOB STATE COMMAND PORT LOAD

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.lineage: Spectrogram plate on a light box
options.thesis: Commands as hairline emission lines on one rail; state as line height, dash, doubling.
options.viewport: A single rail with a tick per command; the open one blooms into a plate.
options.risk: Beautiful but abstract; you'd decode lines instead of reading names.
options.case: Loses both axes: devs don't identify with spectra, and names hide behind ticks.
options.kept: State carried by form, not hue alone.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A visible construction grid with monumental grid-built letterforms.
options.viewport: Giant & built from cells over a small status grid.
options.case: Loses both axes in a 360pt popover.
options.kept: One strict field grid every row obeys.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Flat colour tiles and giant cropped lowercase; chrome deleted.
options.viewport: A tile per command, live tiles flip with CPU.
options.case: Loses both axes: un-Mac, and tiles hide dense status.
options.kept: Chrome deletion: type and state are the interface.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.viewport: A small sky with one star per command.
options.risk: Spatial metaphor with no spatial truth.
options.case: Loses both axes: position means nothing for processes.
options.kept: One ranked magnitude ramp for load.

options.label: Factory Catalog
options.lineage: Peter Saville / Factory Records FAC numbers
options.thesis: Every artifact gets a catalog number; colour codes stand in for words.
options.viewport: FAC-numbered index, one pulse plot owning the field.
options.case: Loses both axes: decoding is the opposite of glanceable.
options.kept: Catalog numbers as identity (%1, %2 job numbers).

canonCard.label: Native macOS utility
canonCard.thesis: What Mac menu bar utilities ship: Control Center-style rows, SF Symbols, green/red dots, executed with full HIG craft.
canonCard.viewport: Popover with grouped rows: status dot, name, port, toggle switch; window is a sidebar + log detail.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other menu bar utility by design.
